_comment: AI/LLM/vector-DB exposure probes. Each probe verifies that a previously-classified AI service accepts requests WITHOUT authentication. A success match means the endpoint is publicly queryable — this is emitted as a Finding with the specified severity. Probes are intentionally read-only and use empty/minimal bodies; they must never trigger inference, write data, or cost money. Success criteria live under `success_when`: status_in (HTTP status whitelist) plus at least one of body_contains (substring whitelist) or body_contains_any (substring whitelist — any one wins). Probes should match the *unauthenticated-and-responsive* shape, NOT the *exploited* shape.

probes.name: ollama-unauth-tags
probes.title: Ollama API accessible without authentication
probes.description: The Ollama inference server exposes /api/tags without any authentication. An attacker can list loaded models, pull new ones, execute arbitrary inference (incurring GPU cost), or exfiltrate model data. Ollama has no built-in auth and should never be exposed to the public internet.

probes.name: ollama-unauth-generate
probes.title: Ollama /api/generate accepts unauthenticated requests
probes.description: POST /api/generate on the Ollama server responds to unauthenticated callers (empty body returns a 400 complaining about missing fields rather than 401/403). An attacker can submit inference jobs, consume GPU resources, and potentially trigger prompt-injection against any loaded model.

probes.name: qdrant-unauth-collections
probes.title: Qdrant vector DB accessible without API key
probes.description: The Qdrant /collections endpoint returns a 200 without an API key header. An attacker can enumerate collections, read embeddings (potentially leaking training data or PII), and write/delete vectors. Qdrant's API key is opt-in and is clearly not configured here.

probes.name: milvus-unauth-describe
probes.title: Milvus HTTP API accessible without authentication
probes.description: The Milvus HTTP proxy responds to /v1/vector/collections/describe without authentication. An attacker can enumerate vector collections, describe their schemas, and issue queries against stored embeddings.

probes.name: chroma-unauth-collections
probes.title: Chroma vector DB accessible without authentication
probes.description: The Chroma /api/v1/collections endpoint returns a 200 without any auth token. Chroma by default has no authentication; an attacker can list collections, read embeddings, and insert or delete vectors.

probes.name: vllm-unauth-models
probes.title: vLLM / OpenAI-compatible API accessible without authentication
probes.description: The /v1/models endpoint returns a 200 without requiring an Authorization header. An attacker can enumerate loaded models and submit inference requests to /v1/chat/completions, consuming GPU resources. If --api-key was intended on vLLM, it is not enforced on this deployment.

probes.name: vllm-unauth-chat-completions
probes.title: vLLM / OpenAI-compatible /v1/chat/completions accepts unauthenticated requests
probes.description: POST /v1/chat/completions with an empty body returns 400/422 (missing field) rather than 401/403, confirming the endpoint does not require authentication. An attacker can submit arbitrary prompts, consume GPU resources, and attempt prompt-injection attacks.

probes.name: mcp-unauth-tools-list-streamable
probes.title: MCP server exposes tools/list without authentication
probes.description: The Model Context Protocol server at /mcp responds to a JSON-RPC tools/list call without any auth. MCP servers often wrap filesystem, shell, database, or API tools — exposing them unauthenticated gives an attacker a remote tool-use harness. This is typically an internal development server that was never meant to be reachable from the internet.

probes.name: mcp-unauth-tools-list-sse
probes.title: MCP SSE transport exposed without authentication
probes.description: The MCP server's legacy /sse transport responds to a GET without any auth, advertising a messages endpoint for subsequent JSON-RPC calls. An attacker can open a session and invoke tools/list + tools/call against whatever tools the server exposes.

probes.name: litellm-unauth-key-info
probes.title: LiteLLM /key/info accessible without authentication
probes.description: LiteLLM's /key/info endpoint returns a 200 without a master key. An attacker can enumerate virtual keys, inspect spend/usage, and — if the same weakness extends to admin endpoints — rotate keys or drain credits. The master key is almost certainly misconfigured on this deployment.

probes.name: langserve-unauth-invoke
probes.title: LangServe /invoke accessible without authentication
probes.description: POST /invoke on this LangServe deployment responds to unauthenticated calls (empty input returns validation error rather than 401/403). An attacker can submit arbitrary inputs to the chain, consume LLM tokens, and attempt prompt-injection against any tools wired into the chain.
